area: Enemy AI: attack tokens, cadence, telegraphs

item_verdicts.title: Attack token / combat-director pattern (DOOM token pool, slot systems)
item_verdicts.why: Sources check out: the Thompson article verbatim confirms per-attack-type token pools ("each type of attack ... has a limited number of tokens available", "A demon needs to request a token to make their attack, then release the token back"), token stealing ("demons can actually steal tokens from one another"), and difficulty-scaled pool counts. Vossen verbatim: "Most games have a slot system to control which enemy attacks when" and "Only enemies from the near group actually attack the player, with enemies from the far group may sparingly use ranged attacks." The GitHub token repo exists as described. Repo side is fully verified: AISeamController.ts lines 21-24 do assert "NO ATTACK TOKEN ... EMERGENT from independent AI_THINK_INTERVAL_MS timers plus the narrow AI_MELEE_RANGE gate"; ai.ts AI_MELEE_RANGE comment repeats it; mobs.ts ENCOUNTER_SIZE = 8; EncounterScene.ts:77 wires all 8 mobs to AISeamController(AI_TIERS.normal); ledger gap-H row says verbatim "enemies take TURNS — 1 at a time (occasionally 2) ... Implement an attack token"; and grep finds NO test anywhere asserting simultaneous-attacker count, so the emergence claim is genuinely untested. The adjudication is STRENGTHENED by a file the research did not cite: src/core/Sim.ts (enemy loop) states "two mobs committing on the same frame is allowed — and A6 measures that it actually happens" — the repo already concedes the failure mode. Only the universality sentence overreaches beyond what any source supports.
item_verdicts.correction: Replace "Nobody ships turn-taking as an emergent side effect of independent timers; it is always an explicit, testable cap" with: "Vossen reports that MOST games use an explicit slot/token cap; no source surveyed claims universality, and none tests the emergent-timer alternative." Also loosen the attribution: the token-pool description is Tommy Thompson's Game Developer write-up, which credits Campbell's 2017 GDC talk and Loudy's 2018 talk elsewhere in the piece but does NOT source the token system to either — cite it as Thompson, not "per Loudy/Campbell GDC material". The ADAPT verdict, the gate-first plan, and the single-token design all stand unchanged, and Sim.ts's own "two mobs committing on the same frame is allowed — and A6 measures that it actually happens" comment should be quoted as supporting evidence.

item_verdicts.title: Two-case telegraph (600 ms approach / 267 ms point-blank), no telegraph VFX
item_verdicts.why: Every element re-checked at the files. src/config/ai.ts: AI_TELEGRAPH_MS = { closing: 600, pointBlank: 267 } as const, labeled CONTRACT-SRC, with the header comment confirming the old per-tier telegraphMs was deleted in SESSION13 D8; AI_POINT_BLANK_X = 25 is labeled INFERRED with an explicit "the boundary between them is not [measured]" note and a veto line. AISeamController.next() selects it exactly as described: `dist <= AI_POINT_BLANK_X ? AI_TELEGRAPH_MS.pointBlank : AI_TELEGRAPH_MS.closing` at commit time. Ledger gap-H rows verbatim: "telegraph, approach attack | 0.600 s", "telegraph, point-blank repeat | 0.267 s ... A single global >=520 ms telegraph is wrong; the OG has two cases", and "telegraph FX | none — pose change only. Do NOT give enemies a drawn stroke line" — the guard rail is quoted correctly. Neither row appears in the §00b corrections table nor in the §S24-H verify-pass block. Sources hold: GDKeys states verbatim "Anticipation time = (player's reaction time) + (expected player's ability trigger time) + (difficulty buffer)" and "the reaction time of a player will be 0.25 seconds", with the Hornet per-move breakdown (Dash 15f, Throw 20f, Lasso 20f, Dive long). Nothing to correct.

item_verdicts.title: Blocking the OG doesn't have — the flagged AISeamController blocking is already deleted
item_verdicts.why: All four repo assertions verified. src/core/OpponentController.ts carries the explicit deletion block "THE react() SEAM IS DELETED (SESSION13 D8) ... measured: zero blocking across the study corpus"; src/config/ai.ts header lists reactMs/reactBlockChance/reactDodgeChance as removed and notes reactMs's cadence role moved to AI_THINK_INTERVAL_MS; AISeamController.ts contract repeats it; and tests/Sim.test.ts plants a controller that still defines `react: () => 'block'` and asserts `drainEvents().filter((e) => e.type === 'strikeBlocked')` equals [] plus identical damage/hp/combo vs a clean sim — exactly the chaos-test shape claimed. grep for strikeBlocked returns only three hits: the SimEvent union member in src/core/Sim.ts, the empty branch in src/game/DuelScene.ts:519, and the negative assertion in tests — it is never emitted anywhere, so "the type exists to power the negative assertion" and "DuelScene's handler is dead render code" are both literally true. Ledger gap-H row verbatim: "block / parry / dodge | NONE in ~70 s across ~30 enemies — clean negative", and it even names AISeamController.react() as the offender, matching the stale-flag diagnosis. Vossen supports the optional framing ("In some games enemies also have the ability to respond to the player's attacks with a block, dodge, or counter attack").

item_verdicts.title: Gait split + speed retune: trash walks ~128 stage px/s, bosses ONLY run — single ENEMY_SPEED is wrong on both counts
item_verdicts.why: Core is solid and the arithmetic is right. src/config/ai.ts ENEMY_SPEED = 0.1417 world px/ms with provenance "Was 0.17 stage px/ms (= 170 stage px/s → 141.67 world px/s)" — 170 stage px/s sits above gap-H's measured 105-161 band and is 1.33x the 128 median, exactly as claimed; ai.ts exports no boss/enemy run speed at all, confirming "no boss approach speed". gap-H rows verbatim: "walk speed | median 128 stage px/s (105-161 across 8 enemies)", the ~22 px/tick peak correction with its "~25 % too fast" wording, and "approach gait | walk only ... the deep-lean run is used only as the attack lunge". §S24-D's boss correction is verbatim: "Honda NEVER walked — all 5 non-dash legs (approach AND retreat) are deep-lean runs at 573-716 ... trash walks · bosses run · both dash only as attack openers", and it explicitly cross-checks MOVE_RUN_PX_S 288 world = 648 @1080 as in-band (confirmed present in src/config/combat-sim.ts). What moves is the boss band's top: the §S24-H verify-pass block (2026-08-12, published after the research ran) narrows it.
item_verdicts.correction: BOSS_RUN_SPEED band: use 255-304 world px/s (573-685 px/s @1080), not 255-318 (573-716). §S24-H verify-pass correction #5 states: "§S24-D: run core quoted 573-685 px/s @1080 (endpoint sensitivity); the bimodal empty-middle claim stands as stated only for whole-leg averages — say so wherever it is cited." So (a) drop the 716 max-medium top, and (b) when justifying the gait picker keying on speed alone, note that the "no leg in 300-500 px/s" empty middle holds for leg AVERAGES only — per-tick instantaneous speeds alternate ~382-435 / ~800-860 inside every run leg, so a per-tick speed threshold would flap. MOVE_RUN_PX_S 288 world (648 @1080) remains in-band under the narrowed range; MOB_WALK_SPEED ~= 106.7 world px/s is unaffected.

item_verdicts.title: Enemy attack = dash-THROUGH (commit ~194 stage px, resolve ~96 px PAST), not a stationary strike inside a 50-px gate
item_verdicts.why: The diagnosis is correct and verified. gap-H's attack-geometry row reads verbatim "a dash-THROUGH, the same mechanic as the player: commit at 194 stage px, damage resolves at the END of the dash when the enemy is 96 stage px PAST the player. A radius check cannot reproduce this". The repo is exactly the forbidden radius check: AISeamController gates on `dist < AI_MELEE_RANGE.x && dy < AI_MELEE_RANGE.y` (50/50 world, CONTRACT-SRC per D8), and src/core/Sim.ts carries the quoted comment "Enemy strike: telegraph timing/range are the CONTROLLER's job" above executeStrike(), which resolves damage in place with zero enemy translation. §S24-E is real and flagged "A12.2 input"; the gap-K tension (approach-run harmless, only the dash phase damages) is quoted accurately. Two problems. (1) The §S24-H verify-pass block re-specifies the dash model the note says to reuse. (2) The grade-A GDC Vault source is real ("Bringing Hell to Life: AI and Full Body Animation in 'DOOM'", Jake Campbell, id Software) but PAYWALLED, and its public abstract covers animation quality selling stylized characters — it does not state the "attacks are commitments the AI cannot take back / the attack IS a movement" framing attributed to it, so that sentence is unverifiable.
item_verdicts.correction: Two fixes. (1) Dash model: §S24-H verify-pass correction #4 wins — "model the dash as a constant-speed line-follow ~616 px/s @1080 (~274 world px/s), range ~40-49 px/tick + the terminal contact snap (+139-192 px, one tick) ... build the Sim mover constant-speed at 60 Hz; compare fidelity at capture level (15 fps sampling) ... Do NOT hand-author a 27/55 stepper into core." So drop "reuse the §S24-E stepper" (there is no stepper to reuse) and do NOT hard-code the flat 403 world px/s lunge: the ledger now carries three non-reconciled dash speeds — gap-H's enemy lunge 484 stage px/s (403 world), §S24-E's corrected player line-follow ~274 world px/s, and §S24-D's terminal dash-lunge cluster 1251-1860 px/s @1080 (556-827 world, 1-2 ticks only). Treat "enemy lunge == player dash" as an OPEN question to measure, not an assumption, and model the enemy attack as line-follow + terminal contact snap so the terminal-tick damage falls out of the snap. (2) Demote the DOOM GDC talk to non-load-bearing: it is paywalled and its abstract does not support the attack-commitment framing; the ledger rows alone carry this item.

item_verdicts.title: Per-enemy attack cadence: validate against the measured 0.467-1.933 s landed-hit band, not the genre's 2-3 s default
item_verdicts.why: Every number re-read at source. src/config/ai.ts AI_TIERS: easy 180/760, normal 180/620, hard 160/480 — exactly as quoted; AI_THINK_INTERVAL_MS = 500 (CONTRACT-SRC D7/D8); AI_RECOVER_JITTER_FRAC = 0.35; the file header still says values are "spec-EXACT", and D8's edits removed only telegraphMs and the three react fields, so "spec-era, never reconciled against gap-H" is accurate. Ledger gap-H cadence row verbatim: "cadence (landed hits) | min 0.467 s, median 0.733 s, mean 0.853 s, max 1.933 s (n=10)" — not touched by §00b or the §S24-H verify-pass block. The Vossen genre default is verbatim: "In most of the games I looked at, an enemy attacks the player every two-to-three seconds on average" — so the ~3x-slowdown framing is fair against a 0.733 s median. The "no test asserts the composed inter-hit distribution" claim survives: grep across tests/ finds no landed-hit inter-arrival assertion; tests/AISeamController.test.ts's "decision cadence" block only proves rolls happen once per beat rather than per tick. The cited harness pattern is real — tests/harness.test.ts runs 24 seeds and asserts the median inside DUEL_TARGET_SECONDS {min: 8, max: 25}. The sequencing advice (tune after the dash-through rework) is sound since attack travel time composes into the interval.

overall_note: Attacked all six items across sources, repo, and ledger; nothing was refuted. Source integrity is good: all four spot-checked URLs resolve and three of them (Thompson/DOOM, Vossen, GDKeys) say verbatim what is attributed to them, including the exact quotes the research leaned on. The one soft spot is the grade-A GDC Vault talk — real, correctly titled and attributed to Jake Campbell/id Software, but paywalled, so the \"attacks are full-body commitments the AI cannot take back\" framing in item 5 cannot be verified from its public abstract and should not be load-bearing. Repo verification: every ALREADY_DONE is genuinely present (two-case telegraph wired through AI_POINT_BLANK_X; react() seam deleted with a planted-controller chaos test asserting strikeBlocked never fires), and every ADAPT's cited defect is real (ENEMY_SPEED above the measured walk band with no boss speed at all; executeStrike resolving in place with no travel; no test anywhere asserting simultaneous-attacker count or landed-hit inter-arrival). One piece of evidence the research MISSED strengthens item 1 rather than weakening it: src/core/Sim.ts's enemy loop already concedes \"two mobs committing on the same frame is allowed — and A6 measures that it actually happens\", which contradicts the AISeamController header's emergent-turn-taking defence from inside the repo. Ledger verification: gap-H rows for telegraph, telegraph FX, block/parry/dodge, cadence, walk speed and attack geometry all read exactly as quoted, and none appear in the §00b overturned table. Three items are WEAKENED, two of them purely by the §S24-H \"Verify-pass corrections (2026-08-12)\" block that postdates the research — boss run band narrows 255-318 to 255-304 world px/s and the bimodal empty middle is leg-averages-only (item 4), and the dash must be built as a constant-speed ~274 world px/s line-follow plus terminal contact snap with no hand-authored 27/55 stepper (item 5). Item 1's weakening is the research's own: \"nobody ships / it is always\" is an absolute no source supports — Vossen says \"most games\". Priority ordering stands: item 1's gate-first harness is the cheapest high-value next move, and item 6 must wait for item 5 as the research itself argues.
